subject: Operational constraints & decision canvas: private VPC / on‑prem hosting
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-04-12T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Operational constraints & decision canvas: private VPC / on‑prem hosting

Team —

I'm pulling together a short decision canvas for the upcoming product/ops review on 4/19. The ask: we need a crisp summary of the minimal architecture patterns and the resourcing implications for 2 runway options so leadership can pick a path (Pilot + hardened pilot vs Full gated GA). Specifically I need:

- A concise list of architecture constraints we cannot waive (networking/KMS/audit log retention)
- Minimum cross‑functional headcount for pilot (SRE + infra + security + release owner) and an estimate for GA staffing
- Any procurement or vendor approvals we should queue now (e.g., HSM, storage contracts)
- A short list of criteria that would qualify a customer for the exception lane (what makes an on‑prem or VPC justified vs hosted)

I attached a blank decision canvas (hosting-decision-canvas.xlsx). Please fill the following tabs: "Constraints", "Staffing", "Exception Criteria" — keep bullets and rough numbers only. If you have cost/ops knobs (e.g., quantization/limited KV cache) that change the staffing math, call them out.

Timeline: can you each populate your sections and return by COB 4/16? I'll synthesize and share a one‑pager for the 4/19 review.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Product Director, Private Hosting
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Operational constraints & decision canvas: private VPC / on‑prem hosting

Soojin —

Quick tech notes from infra/architecture perspective (high level):

- Non‑negotiable constraints:
  * KMS key separation and HW‑backed key material for regulated customers (HSM/KMS integration within 2 weeks of pilot signoff)
  * Network segmentation: customer VPC peering or private link + egress control for data residency
  * Audit log retention minimum 90 days with immutable write once storage (longer if required by customer)

- Pilot footprint (minimal):
  * 2 infra engineers (setup & runbook), 1 SRE (run operations), 1 security engineer (integration validations), 1 release owner (product). If the customer needs on‑prem airgapped deploy add 1 infra specialist with offline install experience.
  * Ops: 24/7 coverage via a shared oncall for the first 60 days (rotating between SREs) — GA requires dedicated oncall team.

- GA staffing estimate (per 10 active private customers):
  * 4 infra engineers, 3 SREs, 2 security eng, 1 program manager, 1 escalation manager (for vendor/sales coordination).

- Architecture knobs that alter staffing: smaller KV cache + aggressive batching reduces GPU ingress needs (lowers infra ops work by ~1 FTE across pilot). Heavy audit/retention increases storage ops and monitoring burden.

I'll mark the canvas with these numbers and attach a short list of open technical questions (kms-integration-notes.docx).

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Infra
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-04-13T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operational constraints & decision canvas: private VPC / on‑prem hosting

Thanks for starting this, Soojin. A few compliance/security gating items to call out for the canvas: 

- SOC2 scope: we need to confirm whether the private deployment will be in‑scope for Redwood's SOC2 or covered under the customer's audits. If in‑scope, we must plan evidence collection and controls testing (adds ~2 weeks prep).
- KMS/HSM: vendor procurement timelines vary (HSM orders can be 4–6 weeks plus provisioning). If a customer demands HSM, we should surface this as an exception with associated lead time and cost.
- Data residency: if GreenBank requires long retention + legal hold capabilities we need a data flow map and an SLA for eDiscovery requests.
- Pen test: for on‑prem we should require a pre‑GA penetration test and signoff from our security team.

Action items for the canvas (I will update the "Exception Criteria" tab):
- Add procurement lead times (HSM, FIPS storage)
- Add security gating checklist (SOC2 impact, pen test, KMS SLA)

I don't want to block the 4/19 decision but these items should be explicit so leadership sees the risk/time tradeoffs.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-14T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operational constraints & decision canvas: private VPC / on‑prem hosting

Adding ops/cost perspective — see attached capex-estimate.pdf for a ballpark. Summary below:

- Short pilot (6–8 weeks): incremental infra spend ~$35k (mostly storage, provisioning windows, and one‑time validation effort). Requires 0.5 FTE procurement/ops support for vendor coordination.
- GA (per region): baseline capex ~$220k (N+1), plus ongoing monthly runrate ~ $18k for monitoring + backups + audit storage. These are placeholder numbers — we should lock them soon if leadership wants to greenlight a pilot.

Staffing recommendations (aligned with Karthik):
- Pilot: 1 lead infra eng, 1 ops runbook owner (can be shared across pilots), fractional security (~0.3 FTE), product release owner. Oncall: rotate among SREs with 4 hour SLO during pilot window.
- GA: dedicate 2 infra, 2 SREs per region, 1 escalation/field eng to support customers, 1 program manager for release cadence.

Open operational risks:
- Night‑time escalation for customers in APAC if we do US‑only staffing — requires cross‑region oncall coverage or follow‑the‑sun recruiting.
- Vendor SLAs: HSM vendors vary; we should list preferred vendors and pre‑negotiate terms for latency and replacement timelines.

I'll drop the capex estimate into the Drive folder and mark assumptions in the spreadsheet.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turn here — this is exactly what we needed. Next steps I propose: 

1) I'll synthesize the canvas and circulate a one‑pager to leadership by EOD 4/16 with the three pathways: "Pilot (limited footprint)", "Pilot+Hardened (pre‑GA requirements)" and "GA (full support)".
2) We should book a 45min cross‑functional sync on 4/19 (I'll send an invite). Required attendees: infra, SRE, security, product, legal, CS.
3) Karthik/Jonas — please add your numbers to the canvas and leave comments on assumptions. Kimberly — please add the procurement lead times and security checklist.
4) I'll include a recommended exception criteria flow: customer need (regulated + data residency) + willingness to sign procurement + legal SLA = exception path. The one‑pager will include explicit lead times and cost buckets.

External note: Diana — thanks for the earlier context. If GreenBank has any hard constraints that would push this into the exception lane (e.g., mandatory HSM, legal hold beyond 7 years), please flag those ASAP so we can include in the leadership packet.
